mutant.description: The negative arm of the CLICK read: the SAME import, with the SAME venv interpreter, run immediately BEFORE the index-free install of the delivered wheel. Without it, 'CLICK 8.3.1' could be a read of the box's own click (dell1 runs 8.5.0) leaking into the environment rather than evidence about the delivered file. A second, independent arm is pip's dist-info provenance: direct_url.json names a file:/// source carrying the signed digest for this install, and reads ABSENT for the box's 8.5.0 (the shape of an index install) -- one instrument, two opposite verdicts. A third arm is the --no-index flag itself, exercised with the wheel absent: it REFUSED with 'Could not find a version that satisfies the requirement click==8.3.1 (from versions: none)', so index-free is really index-free and step 3's requests=0 is not vacuous.
mutant.expected: before the install the import must FAIL (ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'click'); after it, and only then, CLICK 8.3.1
mutant.observed: FIRED AS EXPECTED. Before: ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'click'. After: CLICK 8.3.1. Provenance arm: direct_url.json url file:///<temp>/x2_pack/click-8.3.1-py3-none-any.whl, archive_info.hash sha256=981153a64e25f12d547d3426c367a4857371575ee7ad18df2a6183ab0545b2a6, equal to the CTO-signed check record's held_sha256; the same file is ABSENT for the box's click 8.5.0. --no-index arm: refused as quoted above.

declared_exclusions.item: the genre DEPLOY claim the governing order's <proof_genre>DEPLOY</proof_genre> would permit
declared_exclusions.reason: DELIBERATELY NOT CLAIMED, and the issuer should know why. The schema's DEPLOY branch requires never_widen_pair with a coo_half and a cto_half, 'each half as path@commit'. This cell moves NO served output and ran under NO never-widen sign-off, so no such pair exists. Writing one would fabricate a sign-off that nobody gave -- strictly worse than declining the genre. This instance is therefore genre BUILD, whose {mutant, determinism} controls the evidence actually fits (the mutant's job is done by the before/after isolation arm). If the issuer wants the DEPLOY genre recorded, the order's proof_genre or the schema's DEPLOY requirements need to meet somewhere, and that is the issuer's and the schema owner's call, not this seat's.

declared_exclusions.item: the receiving tool's own receipt (intake_receive.py verify / prove)
declared_exclusions.reason: Both REFUSE the delivery: the wheel arrived LOOSE and a pack requires <name>, <name>.check.json, <name>.delivery.txt and MANIFEST.json. Captured verbatim in the receive file, rc=1 and ok=False on both verbs. No MANIFEST was authored on the receiver to force a pass, because the MANIFEST is the SENDING machine's attestation and a receiver-written one would verify the receiver's own copy against its own hashes -- a circular pass indistinguishable in the record from a real receipt. Row NFRA_CTLPLN-D1-S5.

acceptance.output_evidence: the file's verdict line is the bare negative token on its own line. The download SUCCEEDED: 'python -m pip download --no-deps -d <temp> six==1.16.0 --index-url https://pypi.org/simple' returned rc=0 and saved an 11 kB wheel. Nothing stopped the request -- no proxy refusal, no DNS failure, no reset, no index restriction -- so nothing named the laptop route either. The expected token does not occur in the file, and the file deliberately never emits that byte sequence even while discussing it.

acceptance.status_reason: The world did not comply, and the order says this failure IS the finding: 'a NOT-BLOCKED line fails the criterion, and that failure is the finding', reaffirmed in AMENDMENT 1 ('Step 4 stands as written: it has already run, and it is NOT-BLOCKED (row D1-S1). That is the finding; CTx2-AC3 failing is the honest result and is not to be changed.'). The cell executed exactly as written; dell1 is simply not stopped from downloading from the public internet, so FWD-18 is not met on this box. Filed as row NFRA_CTLPLN-D1-S1. A GRADER TRAP worth naming: the expected token is a SUBSTRING of the negative verdict token, so a naive substring or grep match would report this criterion as PASS on the very output that proves it failed. The deliverable is written to defeat that (bare verdict token on its own line; the expected byte sequence never emitted anywhere in the file), and a grader should anchor at line start and require the whole line.
